name: Teatre Poliorama, La Rambla (Orwell's rooftop)
story: George Orwell, on leave from the POUM militia on the Aragon front, spent the May Days of 1937 on the roof of the Poliorama cinema (Rambla 115) guarding the POUM executive building across the Rambla, as he describes in 'Homage to Catalonia'. The Rambla, Plaça de Catalunya and the old city were divided by barricades between CNT/POUM and government/PSUC forces. A month later the POUM was outlawed and Orwell escaped from Spain as its members were being arrested. A small square in the Gothic Quarter, Plaça de George Orwell, now bears his name.
see: The building of the Reial Acadèmia de Ciències i Arts with the Poliorama theatre, its façade and clock tower much as Orwell knew them.
plan: Free, visible from La Rambla; the theatre is open only for performances.
